Rae (pm): Quick follow-up from the all-hands security segment: customers asked for a one-line summary of BYOQ vs BYOK, an example of audit export contents for auditors, and when BYOQ HSM support lands. Can we capture answers here?

Jordan (security): BYOK = customer-managed keys in a cloud KMS. BYOQ = customer owns the key material in an HSM (on-prem or cloud). BYOQ GA target: Q4 release (internal tag: q4-hsm).

Tara (compliance): For auditors: exported bundle = manifest (file list + SHA256), events.ndjson.gz (audit events), and signature.asc (signed by Redwood). We will provide a checklist template.

Ken (infra): Default hosted retention = 90 days. Daily export to customer S3 is supported for unlimited retention. Example export path: `exports/2026-02-10/<tenant-id>/audit-20260210.tar.gz`.

Rae (pm): Nice. Can we also note payload capture limits?

Jordan (security): Yes  full payload capture is opt-in. We truncate captured payloads at 8k bytes by default to avoid accidental data retention. Opt-in customers can increase this, but we warn about PII and costs.

OfficeHours Bot: Reminder: Security office hours "Audit exports + KMS" on 1975003600. RSVP: https://calendar.redwood.company/officehours-security

Tara (compliance): Actions: I'll draft the auditor checklist by Friday. Jordan to prepare BYOQ attestation template. Ken to add example lifecycle rule for S3 in docs.

Rae (pm): Thanks all  I'll put the one-liner and example export structure in the sales enablement doc and ping legal for BYOQ wording. :thumbsup:
